_comment: Concentric-view anchors. The root is a wave propagating outward; everything in this file is constructed in sync_cost/curriculum/01_what_a_wave_is. The six observations are planted (un-named) at the end of that module and named in the (not-yet-written) Module 1a. Each observation links to one or more framework nodes — these IDs MUST exist in derivation-graph.json and the link should be verified before edits.

root.label: wave outward
root.summary: A disturbance propagating from one point to another through a medium with restoring tendency, inertia, and coupling between neighbors. The single object every claim in this graph descends from.

ingredients.label: restoration
ingredients.summary: Near any rest state, the energy is locally a parabola; the restoring force is proportional to displacement. Forced by the local-parabola role planted in Module 0.

ingredients.label: inertia
ingredients.summary: Mass means the medium overshoots when restored. Without it, no oscillation. With it, period 2π·√(m/k).

ingredients.label: coupling
ingredients.summary: A force between neighbors that responds to their *relative* displacement. Translation symmetry of the medium forces this form. What turns a row of oscillators into a wave.

observations.label: Doppler shift
observations.summary: Relative motion between source and observer shifts the measured frequency. Direct from wave-outward + relative motion.

observations.label: redshift
observations.summary: The cosmic-scale version of the same effect: distant sources, receding as the cosmos stretches, are measured at lower frequencies. The shift grows with distance.

observations.label: time dilation
observations.summary: If a wave's propagation speed is the same for every observer, time and distance must be measured differently by different observers. The wave's constancy forces the geometry.

observations.label: E = mc²
observations.summary: A wave confined to a small region carries energy proportional to its frequency of confinement. That confined energy, pinned in place, is what we call mass.

observations.label: Planck wall
observations.summary: The smallest-scale wall. Below this confinement scale, the energy required to localize the wave makes its own gravitational horizon. No wave can be defined further in.

observations.label: Hubble wall
observations.summary: The largest-scale wall. Above this wavelength, the cosmos stretches faster than the wave can complete a cycle. No wave can complete a coherent oscillation further out.

our_band.label: where we live
our_band.summary: Our frequency — sound, light, chemistry, biology — sits decades-deep between the two walls. The behavior at our frequency is extremely stable because we are far from both boundaries; no boundary correction matters at our scale. The framework's dramatic moves happen at the walls; here, locally, the construction simply holds.
